summary: Defines the immutable result types returned by storage metadata, listing and enumeration operations. StorageEntry is a frozen, slotted dataclass describing one file, directory or object-store prefix (path, name, size, last_modified, etag, content_type, entry_type, storage_class, source, version_id, checksum, checksum_algorithm). EnumerateResult pairs a tuple of object entries with a tuple of common-prefix entries for list_objects(). EntryType is a StrEnum of file, directory and prefix.
key_classes: StorageEntry — frozen/slots dataclass: unified descriptor for a file, directory or prefix across all backends
EnumerateResult — frozen/slots dataclass of objects and common_prefixes tuples returned by list_objects()
extension_points: Backend authors populate StorageEntry from native metadata; optional fields default to None/empty string, so a backend fills only what its service reports
lifecycle_notes: Stdlib-only and imported by every backend; immutable values that can outlive the facade that produced them
documentation_hooks: Reference page for StorageEntry fields with per-backend population matrix (which backends set etag, version_id, checksum, storage_class, content_type)
list_objects() result semantics: objects vs common_prefixes, shared max_results limit, delimiter behaviour (README exact-path and S3 prefix enumeration sections)
Timestamp semantics: last_modified is UTC-aware on Local and SFTP; None when the server omits it
examples: examples/local_files/example.py — reads StorageEntry from metadata() and checks entry_type is EntryType.FILE
examples/directories/example.py — list_dir() returning StorageEntry values and reading .name
risks: Empty-string defaults for etag/content_type/version_id/checksum make 'unknown' indistinguishable from an empty value, unlike size/last_modified which use None
SFTP metadata falls back to EntryType.FILE when the server omits mode bits, so FILE is not proof of a regular file (README filesystem directory semantics)
No per-backend contract states which optional fields are populated; consumers may rely on fields that only some backends fill
